The clause now names /legion/scratch/cache, /legion/scratch/tmp, /legion/scratch/bun/install/cache, /legion/go and /legion/uv, keeps the per-role state home named as small and not a cache, and says why tmp cannot be left out: a role at the merge base is told no TMPDIR, so a killed build's residue died with its container, where here it lives as long as the issue. proof.criterion: An operator's reclaim under a running install can no longer leave the issue in a state only a person can clear.
proof.surface: The rendered install block's own shell fragment, executed on this pod's /usr/bin/flock.
proof.command: flock -w 1 -- ./missing true; stat -c '%F' ./missing; ( set -eu; cache=./cachefile; mkdir -p -- "$cache" ); ( set -eu; cache=./cachefile; legion_install() { [ -d "$cache" ] || rm -f -- "$cache"; mkdir -p -- "$cache"; /usr/bin/flock -w 1 -- "$cache" true; }; legion_install || legion_install )
proof.observed: flock on a missing path exits 0 and leaves a regular empty file, which is the state the tester's delete-mid-install rig produces. Over that file the old shape (mkdir outside legion_install) exits 1 with `mkdir: Already exists` under set -eu, before any agent, and would do so on every later installing launch of the issue. The new shape — `[ -d "$cache" ] || rm -f -- "$cache"` then `mkdir -p` inside legion_install, before each attempt's lock — clears exactly that file, reaches the install, exits 0, and leaves the path a directory; an attempt whose cache was deleted after a previous one remakes it and locks the real directory, exit 0. plugins.go:218-230, with the invariant comment rewritten to say why the mkdir is inside and what the outside shape costs.
proof.negativeControl: The same runs with the rm -f guard dropped reproduce `mkdir: Already exists`, exit 1 — so the guard, not the move alone, is what clears the stale file; and the move alone is what makes a deleted cache recoverable on the retry.

proof.criterion: Nothing else at this head moved, and the package still builds and passes.

The live six-role delete-mid-install race is the tester's rig and is not claimed here.

filesChanged: docs/kubernetes.md — the reclaim clause names every directory the layout creates, says why /legion/scratch/tmp is this layout's own new failure mode, and gives the lock reason for deleting between turns.

packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/plugins.go — installBlock makes $BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR inside legion_install before each attempt's lock, after removing a non-directory at that path; the invariant comment says why.
trickyParts: flock creates a missing lock path as a regular file and exits 0. That is why a mkdir outside the retry is a one-way failure rather than a transient one: the file persists, and every later installing launch of the issue dies at mkdir under set -eu until a person removes it.
The removal is scoped to a non-directory at exactly $BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR. A directory there is never removed, so no cache is ever destroyed by the guard.
discoveredComplexity: The round-17 finding is the round-16 finding at one more remove: my own proof's `observed` listed four shared directories from the renderer — cache, data, tmp, bun/install/cache — and the clause I then wrote carried two of them, with no sentence saying why the others were out. The observation was right and the conclusion dropped part of it, which no re-reading of the clause finds; only reading the clause back against the observation that produced it does.

A third mis-authored commit landed this round and the tester reported it against itself (7e9f3f08131f, authored legion-implementer[bot]; handoff_complete refused it and it re-committed as 2b113adafff9). The rule's sharper form: in a workspace six roles share, the guard is not `is the working copy clean` but `is @ mine`, and it must run before anything — another role included — writes. The same defect lost an uncommitted retro learning of mine into the tester's split; the architect recovered it from jj's operation log with `jj --at-op <op> file show`.
